# Skeleton

Figma: [05e. Skeleton](https://www.figma.com/design/a7Z956YZy9n6f9uz5DK16Y?node-id=69-926) · Family: 05 Feedback · Status: stable · Version 2.0.0 · Updated 2026-06-09

Loading placeholders shown while data is being fetched. Skeletons are primitives - SkeletonLine, SkeletonBlock, SkeletonCircle, SkeletonAvatar - that designers compose into the shape of the content being loaded. They use a neutral bg/disabled fill and a subtle shimmer animation (implemented in code, not Figma). 4 primitive components totaling 37 variants. Domain-specific patterns (Deal Card, List Row, Stat Tile, KYC Step) will be added later when the underlying product components exist - building skeletons before their real components leads to drift. NEW in Syntropy v2.0 (no direct legacy counterpart).

Reference image (every variant, labelled): `knowledge/examples/components/skeleton/reference.png`

### SkeletonLine

Pill-shaped grey placeholder for a text line while data loads, sized to the text it replaces (Small 12 to XLarge 28) at Full, 3Q, Half, Quarter or Auto width.

Level: atom

Use when:
- Deal title and subtitle lines while CardDeal data loads
- Label, big value and delta lines of a Stat tile recipe
- Rows of a transaction or payout list during fetch

Don't use when:
- After load with zero items: use EmptyState
- Work with no predictable layout (submitting, processing): use SpinnerRing
- Button submitting: use Button loading state
- Measurable progress: use ProgressBar

Accessibility: Container gets aria-busy=true and a single "Loading" label; shimmer off under prefers-reduced-motion.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Size | `size` | variant | Small, MD, Large, XLarge | Small |
| Width | `width` | variant | Full, 3Q, Half, Quarter, Auto | Full |

### SkeletonBlock

Rectangular placeholder for images, charts, cards or buttons during loading, with Radius None to XLarge matching the real element.

Level: atom

Use when:
- Deal cover image area while CardDeal loads
- Chart area placeholder before data arrives
- Button or card surface shapes in a loading composition

Don't use when:
- Text lines: use SkeletonLine
- Round icons or dots: use SkeletonCircle
- Avatars: use SkeletonAvatar
- Chart card that is loading inside its own chrome: use Chart / States State=loading

Accessibility: Decorative inside an aria-busy container; match the real size to avoid layout shift.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Radius | `radius` | variant | None, Small, Medium, Large, XLarge | None |

### SkeletonCircle

Circular placeholder from 16 to 72px for icons, status dots or small round elements while loading.

Level: atom

Use when:
- Icon slots in list rows or ActionTile grids during loading
- Small round markers in a loading layout
- Round elements up to 72px

Don't use when:
- User or company avatars: use SkeletonAvatar
- Text: use SkeletonLine

Accessibility: Decorative inside an aria-busy container.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Size | `size` | variant | XS, S, M, L, XL, XXL | XS |

### SkeletonAvatar

Avatar-shaped placeholder at S, M, L in Circle (people) or Square (organizations) while profile data loads.

Level: atom

Use when:
- Avatar slot of a comment or notification row recipe
- Developer company logo slot (Shape=Square) on a loading deal card
- Account header loading

Don't use when:
- Generic round icons: use SkeletonCircle
- A loaded user without a photo: use Avatar Type=Initials
- Avatar data loading inside Avatar itself: Avatar Type=Placeholder is also valid

Accessibility: Decorative inside an aria-busy container.

| Property in Figma | Code name | Type | Values | Default |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Size | `size` | variant | S, M, L | S |
| Shape | `shape` | variant | Circle, Square | Circle |

## Guide from the doc page

### Overview

Skeletons are loading placeholders shown while data is being fetched from the network. They convey "content is coming" by mimicking the rough shape of what is about to appear - gray pill-shaped bars where text lines will be, gray rectangles where images will be, gray circles where avatars will be. Unlike spinners (05f, DEFERRED) which communicate "something is happening" abstractly, skeletons preserve the layout shape so the page does not visibly reflow when content lands.

### When to reach for Skeleton

- A list, table, or grid is loading and you know the rough shape of what is coming.
- A card or panel is being fetched (deal card, statement row, portfolio tile).
- A profile, settings page, or any structured screen with predictable layout is loading.
- When you want to preserve perceived performance - skeletons feel faster than spinners because users see content shape immediately.

### When NOT to use Skeleton

- Indeterminate background work (saving, uploading, processing) - use Loader/Spinner (05f).
- Initial app boot or splash - use a branded loading screen.
- Submitting a form - use button-internal loading state (Button has State=loading).
- When the load is genuinely fast (under 200ms) - skeletons cause flicker. Show real content directly.
- When the content shape is unpredictable - a wall of mismatched skeletons looks worse than a centered spinner.

### Anatomy - 4 primitives

Skeleton ships as 4 primitive components. Designers compose them into product-specific patterns inside their own product files. Once the real product components exist (Deal Card, List Item, Stat Tile, KYC Step), a small library of canonical skeleton patterns will be added here as a second layer.

### SkeletonLine

20 variants (4 sizes × 5 widths)

A pill-shaped placeholder for text. Size matches the text size: Small=12px, MD=16px, Large=20px, XLarge=28px. Width: Full (100%), 3Q (75%), Half (50%), Quarter (25%), Auto (designer drags freely). Cornerradius is height/2 so it stays pill-shaped at any width.

### SkeletonBlock

5 variants (Radius: None / Small 4 / Medium 8 / Large 12 / XLarge 16)

A rectangular placeholder for images, charts, or card surfaces. Designer resizes the instance to fit the target. The 5 radius variants match the Syntropy radius scale.

### SkeletonCircle

6 variants (Size: XS 16 / S 24 / M 32 / L 40 / XL 56 / XXL 72)

A perfect circle placeholder for icons, status dots, or small avatar-like elements. Different from SkeletonAvatar in that Circle stops at 72px - for larger avatars or for square avatars, use SkeletonAvatar.

### SkeletonAvatar

6 variants (Size: S 32 / M 40 / L 56) × (Shape: Circle / Square)

Opinionated avatar placeholder covering the most common avatar use case. Circle for user profile photos, Square (with Radius/8) for organization or entity avatars.

### Composition recipes

Skeleton primitives are meant to be composed. Here are 4 generic recipes designers can adapt to their layouts. These are NOT components - they are example compositions that designers should rebuild in their own product files using the primitives.

### Recipe 1 - Avatar row

User row (typically a notification, comment, or contact). Composed of: 1 × SkeletonAvatar (Size=M, Shape=Circle) + 2 × SkeletonLine stacked vertically (a name line and a smaller subtitle line).

### Recipe 2 - Media card

Card with image, title, two body lines, and a button. Composed of: 1 × SkeletonBlock (image, Radius=Medium) + 1 × SkeletonLine (title, Size=Large, Width=3Q) + 2 × SkeletonLine (body, Size=MD, Width=Full and Half) + 1 × SkeletonBlock (button, Radius=Large, custom size).

### Recipe 3 - Stat tile

Stat tile (dashboard tile, portfolio summary, deal stat). Composed of: 1 × SkeletonLine (label, Size=Small, Width=Half) + 1 × SkeletonLine (big value, Size=XLarge, Width=3Q) + 1 × SkeletonLine (delta indicator, Size=Small, Width=Quarter).

### Recipe 4 - List of rows

Vertically stacked rows (account statement, transaction list, settings menu). Reuse Recipe 1 (Avatar row) stacked vertically with a divider between each. Render 4-6 rows for a list to fill the viewport - too few rows feels sparse, too many feels excessive.

### Animation - shimmer behavior

Skeletons animate with a subtle shimmer - a soft highlight that sweeps horizontally across each skeleton surface every 1.4 seconds. The animation conveys "this is alive, content is loading" without distracting. In Figma the skeletons are static; the animation is implemented in code. The showcase below demonstrates the gradient position at each step of the sweep.

Shimmer animation - frame sequence

Skeletons in code animate via a linear-gradient sweep across the surface. These 4 frames show the gradient position at each step of the animation - at rest, left, middle, right. In real product code use a CSS keyframe animation (or Flutter ShimmerEffect / SkeletonAnimation) sweeping a soft highlight across the bg/disabled surface every 1.4s.

Step 1 - At rest

Step 2 - Sweep starts (10%)

Step 3 - Sweep middle (50%)

Step 4 - Sweep ends (90%)

> **Info:** In Flutter, use the shimmer package or skeletonizer. In React, use react-loading-skeleton or implement with a CSS keyframe animation:  @keyframes shimmer { 0% { background-position: -200% 0; } 100% { background-position: 200% 0; } } applied to a background-image of linear-gradient(90deg, transparent 25%, rgba(255,255,255,0.5) 50%, transparent 75%). Duration: 1.4s. Easing: ease-in-out.

> **Tip:** Skeletons should pulse, not blink. Use opacity 0.4 → 0.8 for the highlight, not 0 → 1. A harsh blink reads as broken; a gentle pulse reads as "loading".

> **Warning:** Disable the shimmer animation if the user has prefers-reduced-motion enabled. The static gray skeleton alone is sufficient to communicate "loading" - the shimmer is a polish layer, not the core signal.

### Code examples - Flutter

### Basic primitives

```dart
// SkeletonLine - for text
SkeletonLine(size: SkeletonSize.medium, width: SkeletonWidth.full)
SkeletonLine(size: SkeletonSize.medium, width: SkeletonWidth.threeQuarter)
SkeletonLine(size: SkeletonSize.small, width: SkeletonWidth.half)

// SkeletonBlock - for images, charts, surfaces
SkeletonBlock(width: 240, height: 120, radius: SkeletonRadius.medium)

// SkeletonCircle - for icons, dots
SkeletonCircle(size: 32)

// SkeletonAvatar - opinionated avatar
SkeletonAvatar(size: SkeletonAvatarSize.medium, shape: SkeletonAvatarShape.circle)
```

### Composition: avatar row

```dart
class UserRowSkeleton extends StatelessWidget {
  const UserRowSkeleton({super.key});
  
  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return Padding(
      padding: const EdgeInsets.symmetric(horizontal: 16, vertical: 12),
      child: Row(children: [
        const SkeletonAvatar(
          size: SkeletonAvatarSize.medium,
          shape: SkeletonAvatarShape.circle,
        ),
        const SizedBox(width: 12),
        Expanded(child: Column(
          crossAxisAlignment: CrossAxisAlignment.start,
          children: const [
            SkeletonLine(size: SkeletonSize.medium, width: SkeletonWidth.threeQuarter),
            SizedBox(height: 6),
            SkeletonLine(size: SkeletonSize.small, width: SkeletonWidth.half),
          ],
        )),
      ]),
    );
  }
}
```

### Composition: list of skeleton rows

```dart
class TransactionListSkeleton extends StatelessWidget {
  final int count;
  const TransactionListSkeleton({super.key, this.count = 6});
  
  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) {
    return ListView.builder(
      itemCount: count,
      itemBuilder: (_, __) => const UserRowSkeleton(),
    );
  }
}

// Usage:
StreamBuilder<List<Transaction>>(
  stream: transactionsStream,
  builder: (context, snapshot) {
    if (!snapshot.hasData) return const TransactionListSkeleton();
    return TransactionList(items: snapshot.data!);
  },
)
```

### Shimmer animation wrapper

```dart
// In a SyntropyTheme provider, wrap any skeleton tree with Shimmer:
Shimmer(
  baseColor: theme.bg.disabled,  // Color/Neutral/200
  highlightColor: Colors.white.withOpacity(0.6),
  period: const Duration(milliseconds: 1400),
  child: child,
)

// Or in CSS for web:
.skeleton {
  background: linear-gradient(
    90deg,
    var(--bg-disabled) 0%,
    var(--bg-disabled) 40%,
    rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.6) 50%,
    var(--bg-disabled) 60%,
    var(--bg-disabled) 100%
  );
  background-size: 200% 100%;
  animation: shimmer 1.4s ease-in-out infinite;
}
@keyframes shimmer {
  0% { background-position: 200% 0; }
  100% { background-position: -200% 0; }
}
@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) {
  .skeleton { animation: none; }
}
```

### Notes from the maintainer

> **Info:** Skeleton is NEW in Syntropy v2.0. The legacy Global_Design_System had no dedicated skeleton component - loading states were handled ad-hoc with custom gray rectangles or spinners.

> **Warning:** No domain-specific skeleton patterns (Deal Card, List Item, Stat Tile, KYC Step) are shipped yet. These will be added as a second layer once the underlying real components exist. Building skeletons before their real counterparts leads to drift - the skeleton ends up not matching the real layout. Compose your own from primitives in product files until then.

> **Info:** Use bg/disabled (Color/Neutral/200, rgb 225, 228, 227) as the skeleton fill. There is no dedicated bg/skeleton token in v2.0.0 - if we add one later, the primitives will be updated centrally. Do not hardcode hex values.

> **Warning:** Skeletons should match the SHAPE and SIZE of the content they replace, not be smaller or simpler. If the real card has a 240×120 image area with 12px radius, the skeleton must be 240×120 with 12px radius. If the title line is going to be Large (20px), use Size=Large in the skeleton. Mismatched skeletons cause visible layout shift when content lands.

> **Info:** Pill-shaped lines (radius = height/2) are intentional. Square-edge lines read as broken UI bars; pill-shaped lines read as "text placeholder". This is a Material 3 / iOS convention adopted in Syntropy.

> **Warning:** Do not chain skeleton fade-in/fade-out animations on top of the shimmer. The shimmer alone is enough. Stacking animations causes visual noise and can trigger motion sickness.

> **Tip:** Show skeletons only when load time exceeds 200ms. Below that threshold, the skeleton causes a flash-of-skeleton-content (FOSC) that looks worse than showing nothing. Pair with a 200ms timer: show content if it arrives in under 200ms, otherwise switch to skeleton.

> **Warning:** Do not use skeletons for empty states. Empty states are AFTER load completes with zero items - use EmptyState (05d). Skeletons are DURING load. Confusing the two leads to skeletons that never disappear because there is no data to render.
